turns.answer:
For a position we actually hold, go with the filing for the bank’s modeled rate sensitivity, and use the tape only as a reality check on whether the market is trading that sensitivity cleanly. JPM’s own Item 7 says the earnings-at-risk table is an instantaneous shock model and that actual net interest income may differ because the scenario excludes actions by the Firm or its customers; it also says deposit rates paid and mortgage prepayments may differ from the assumptions, and that the forecast for net interest income sits in the outlook section, not in the sensitivity table ([10-K Item 7], [10-K Item 7], [10-K Item 7]).
What would change the reading is evidence that the filing’s key assumptions are wrong or obsolete: a materially different deposit-beta path, a change in customer deposit behavior, a change in hedge duration or Treasury/CIO actions, or a balance-sheet shift large enough to move the sensitivity table itself. JPM says the recent change in sensitivities was driven mainly by Treasury and CIO actions and firmwide deposits, and that the simulations are periodically evaluated and enhanced as the balance sheet and market conditions change ([10-K Item 7], [10-K Item 7]).
On the tape, the desk’s 1-year TLT adjusted close series is $82.21 (2026-09-04), and the web evidence you asked for shows the market has been trading rate stories in a way that is not the same thing as a bank earnings-at-risk table: one piece says higher long Treasury yields have helped some names that are inversely correlated with TLT, while another says JPMorgan’s own trading desk turned tactically cautious on stocks after hawkish Fed rhetoric, and a third says JPMorgan is still being valued on franchise strength and earnings power, not as a pure duration proxy ([Yields are on the move once again  These stocks could get a boost if they keep going higher - CNBC], [JPMorgan Traders Drop Bullish View on Stocks After Warsh Speech - Bloomberg com], [JPMorgan could soon be the first $1 trillion bank  Top analyst Mayo says next stop is $2 trillion - CNBC]). That is why I would not swap the filing’s model for the tape; I would treat any disagreement as a prompt to test whether the model inputs still fit the book, not as a reason to ignore the model outright.

fact.text: Top analyst Mayo says next stop is $2 trillion. JPMorgan Chase & Co. should get a boost from several tailwinds, enabling it to become the first bank to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization, according to Wells Fargo. Wells has an overweight rating on JPMorgan and recently hiked its price target on the stock to $390 from $375, implying more than 7% upside from Friday's close. "JPMorgan Chase … has excelled at both offense and defense over the past decade, in which it has been gaining market share in all major business lines, while optimizing its businesses, showing consistent earnings relative to other global banks, and creating a 'fortress balance sheet' (as defined by its CEO)," Mayo wrote. $2 trillion Looking farther ahead, JPMorgan could reach a $2 trillion market capitalization in the next seven or eight years, particularly as it deepens its investments across a group of high-growth businesses, according to Wells Fargo. "Achieving $2T market cap requires more EPS growth than re-rating," Mayo wrote, referring to the bank's price-to-earnings ratio and other valuation yardsticks.
